_comment: Acceptance fixtures for prose-medium-critic. Each synthetic fixture is a piece.md and a `form` naming
the medium profile it was made for (staged from prose-author's prose-repurpose skill at prepare time,
the way the structure critic's scan is computed then). The critic receives the profile, the output of
repurpose-check over the piece, and the piece. It never sees this manifest.
`check_says` is the ECHO RULE's verdict (tests/medium-harness.mjs), re-derived by the selftest: what a
critic gets by parroting repurpose-check - any failed mechanical constraint is a REVISE. `class` is the
A  check quiet, critic quiet    - a compliant piece; the critic manufactures nothing
B  check flags, critic quiet    - a mechanical failure is the writer's to fix, not a finding; the critic clears it
C  check flags, critic flags    - an over-length segment that ALSO cuts a sentence: the critic names the cut
D  check quiet, critic flags    - every count passes; only a reader in the medium sees the cut sentence or the buried hook
B and D are the whole argument for the critic existing. The parrot's score is reported beside the critic's.
The leave-one-out negatives are the six shortest Doctorow posts staged under the newsletter profile; every
one is over the profile's word band, so the check says REVISE on all six and the critic must stay quiet where
the count is loud. That is the negative test: compliant human prose as delivery, not whether the critic finds
echo_rule: flagged when repurpose-check reports any mechanical constraint as failed

fixtures.name: n-thread-clean
fixtures.piece_does: Five segments, each under 280 characters, each a whole sentence or two, no link in the first. Nothing to count against and nothing for the medium to break.

fixtures.name: n-thread-long-but-whole
fixtures.piece_does: The first segment is over 280 characters, so the check fails segment-limit. Every segment is whole sentences and stands alone; the length is the writer's to fix, and the critic must not restate the count as a finding.

fixtures.name: p-thread-long-and-cut
fixtures.piece_does: The first segment is over the limit AND ends mid-sentence ('and the / difference is the whole of it'). The check flags the length; the critic must name the cut, which the count cannot see.

fixtures.name: p-thread-cut-sentence
fixtures.piece_does: Every segment is under the limit and there is no link, so the check is quiet. The first separator falls between 'what it was' and 'for.' Only a reader who meets segment one alone sees it.

fixtures.name: n-post-hook-carries
fixtures.piece_does: Under 3,000 characters, no headings, no hashtags; the first line states the piece's claim, so the truncation point carries it.

fixtures.name: p-post-hook-buried
fixtures.piece_does: Same body, but the first two lines are 'a few thoughts... in no particular order' and 'some background first'. Every count passes; the platform truncates after two lines that carry nothing, which is the semantic constraint hook-above-the-fold the check lists as the critic's.

leave_one_out_note: Six posts by one author, staged under the newsletter profile as pieces delivered on the web. All exceed the profile's 1,200-word band, so the parrot scores 0 of 6 on the negatives. Expected CLEAN on all six; <= 1 REVISE is a default, not a measurement (critic-harness.md).
